pairs.why: A's long, trailing, translucent arms and soft glassy bell match the real jellyfish's flowing diagonal silhouette, while B's short bunched ruffles read as a different, stubbier creature.
B keeps the plain dark-navy cylinder with three glowing lenses like the real lamp, while A adds fussy barn-door flaps the real card doesn't have.
B's muted navy body and grey truss match the real card's colour masses, while A's bright yellow toy trim makes it look like a plastic toy.
These are nearly equal, but A's truss running across the frame and its slightly softer, matte navy body sit a bit closer to the real card than B's short boxy truss segment.
B is smoother and cleaner, with flatter colour fills nearer the real map, while A's crinkled paper texture and painted mountains look too textured.
B's thick creamy-white border, saturated green and bold red X match the real card's main colour masses and stiff card-like build better than A's beige crinkled paper.
B has a lighter, cleaner border, fewer creases and a greener face, so it reads closer to the smooth white-edged real maps than A's tan, wrinkled paper.
B's scalloped canopy with the underside showing and its thin pole match the real umbrella's build, while A's fat, glossy, inflated panels and thick pole look like a chunky toy.
